title: latency-stabilizer-and-quantum-reserve-for-dedicated-fleet
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally observe transient tail-latency spikes during short-lived microbursts even when aggregate utilization is within reservation bounds. This leads to SLA churn for customers pinned to dedicated capacity. This PR introduces two coordinated components: 1) a lightweight latency stabilizer in the fleet controller that enforces short-term headroom (the 'quantum reserve') using a bounded, time-decayed reservation escrow; and 2) a congestion-aware shedder that applies proportional shedding and backpressure routing at the gateway when quantum reserve is exhausted. The goal is to keep p99 under SLA without permanently overprovisioning committed capacity.

What I changed: single PR with controller, autoscaler hooks, metric plumbing, and rollout manifests. Implemented a compact in-memory lease escrow (ReservoirQuantum) that tracks short windows of committed headroom, decays allocations over a sliding 15s window, and exposes a per-tenant 'quantum_balance' metric. The stabilizer integrates with the existing dedicate/fleet reconciler to temporarily reserve warm slots for latency-sensitive requests (configurable via TierPolicy). Added a shedder that consumes the same telemetry stream and enforces a proportional shed policy based on latency derivative and quantum_balance. Added telemetry hooks and a dashboard query set for the new metrics.

Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration test: synthetic microburst scenario - [x] Telemetry (Prometheus metrics + Grafana dashboard panels) - [x] Docs: dedicated capacity operator guide (rollout notes) - [x] Feature flag gating (env REDWOOD_ENABLE_QUANTUM_RESERVE)

Testing and validation: Local integration with perf-canary harness (synthetic 100ms baseline, 10s spikes to 3x QPS). Verified headroom decays correctly, quantum_balance avoids oscillation with the tuned decay constant, and p99 improves ~25% under the burst scenario. End-to-end CI run green (unit + integration + e2e smoke). Canary rollout performed on a dedicated staging cluster for 48h with no regressions.

Rollout plan: Feature gated by REDWOOD_ENABLE_QUANTUM_RESERVE; start with opt-in tenants on Dedicated, monitor quantum_balance and p99, gradually widen to default-on for latency-tiered tenants. Fallback: automatic disable if error rate > 1% for 10m.

Operational notes: Added alerting rule that fires when quantum_balance < 10% for > 2m across > 3 tenants (ops:TQuantumLow). Added CI check to ensure telemetry labels (tenant_id, pool_id) are present for new metrics.

Related: ENG-4521 (latency stabilization initiative), ENG-4599 (dedicated SLA improvements).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Overall looks good; a few nits on concurrency safety in quantum_reservoir.go. Can you avoid the double-lock pattern in releaseLease()?
Aisha Kumar: Addressed — switched to per-tenant atomic counters and removed the double-lock in 3rd commit. Added unit tests for concurrent lease churn.
Priya Singh: Need to ensure metric labels include pool_id and tenant_tier (for downstream aggregation). Also: what is the expected cardinality impact?

Aisha Kumar: Metrics include tenant_id, pool_id, tenant_tier. Cardinality kept low by sampling tenant_id only for alerting metrics; standard metrics are aggregated by pool and tier (see quantum_metrics.go comments).
Liam O'Connor: Suggest adding a safety circuit that disables shedder if gateway CPU > 85% to avoid feedback loops.
Aisha Kumar: Added CPU-based kill-switch and documented fallback. Added e2e smoke that triggers the kill-switch path.
Diego Morales: Approved after changes — left an approval on the PR.
Priya Singh: Approved. Please squash commit history before merge.
release_notes: Introduces a short-term headroom mechanism (Quantum Reserve) to stabilize tail latency for Dedicated fleets. Adds a proportional shedding policy and new telemetry (quantum_balance, quantum_consumption) to help ops monitor transient capacity pressure. Feature gated; see docs/operators/dedicated-quantum-reserve.md for rollout and safety procedures.
notes_for_ops: Default off. To enable set REDWOOD_ENABLE_QUANTUM_RESERVE=true in dedicated operator. Monitor ops:TQuantumLow and gateway CPU kill-switch alert. If unexpected throttling occurs, disable flag and contact platform-ops.
backwards_compatibility: no runtime schema changes; API surface is opt-in and backward compatible with existing Dedicated tenants
